passes.intro: A pass is a monthly tab. The price you pay is the money on your tab. Spend it at the pour-list rates. It resets every 30 days. Dry before then? Buy another round.
passes.preOpen: Nothing is for sale tonight. These are the prices at opening. The button puts you on the list and notes which pass you wanted.

well.note: mini and reason think before they answer. Thinking is billed as output, so those two drink faster: about 7 hours at 6k, about 5 at 16k, at about 1,000 thinking tokens a reply.

top.note: The flagship thinks before it speaks and the thinking is billed as output. These hours assume about 1,000 thinking tokens a reply. The same tab pours further down the shelf.
top.button: PUT ME DOWN FOR TOP SHELF

finePrint: A writing hour is counted in 45-minute sessions: about 40 replies of about 400 tokens, each reply inside the minute.
Context is billed every turn, so long contexts and thinking models drink faster. If you run 16k or more of context for hours a day, read the FAQ before you pick a pass.
Pause longer than a minute between messages and the next pour is cold: a wait of about 30 seconds and the cold minimum. The hours above assume you do not.
Rates per shelf are on the pour list. All prices are the whole price, tax excluded.

hasABottom.title: A PASS HAS A BOTTOM.
hasABottom.body: It is a monthly tab in dollars, spent at the pour-list rates. Anyone selling you a bottomless glass is rationing you some other way: one request at a time, a queue, a context cap. We ration with a number you can see.

anotherRound.title: ANOTHER ROUND
anotherRound.headline: Another round: $5 / $10 / $25.
anotherRound.body: Dollar for dollar onto your tab. Poured after the monthly tab runs dry. Good for 12 months. Needs an active pass. No bonus, no bulk price.
anotherRound.preOpen: Rounds open when the bar does.

patron.title: BUY A ROUND FOR THE HOUSE
patron.options: $5 / $10 / $25 / $50 / your call, $5 to $500. Or a standing round: $10 a month, cancel any time.
pitch: You get nothing. No tokens, no priority. Your handle on the wall if you want it.
Someone who could not afford a seat gets one.
patron.unit: $5 is a month at the bar for someone on the community rate.
patron.mechanism: Every dollar goes into the house pool; we pay the card fee. The pool pays us the difference between a reduced price and the standard price, and nothing else. We are a business, not a charity: a round for the house is a payment to a business and is not tax-deductible. If we ever close the programme, what is left goes back to the patrons. From the first round on, the ledger is public and updated monthly: rounds bought, rounds poured, what is left, who is waiting.
patron.refund: Unpoured rounds are refundable on request within 30 days.
patron.preOpen: Rounds for the house open when the bar does. Open a tab and we will tell you.

lastCall.title: LAST CALL
lastCall.headline: The price falls as the bar fills. Here is the schedule. Hold us to it.
rows: 5% lower than the opening rates listed above
15% lower than the opening rates listed above
25% lower than the opening rates listed above
35% lower than the opening rates listed above
rules: The member count is on the status sign. When it holds above a line for two months, rates drop on the 1st of the next month, for everyone, every shelf.
Your pass costs the same. Your tab just pours further. Minimum pours do not change.
A cut stays for at least six months. We only step back if the bar empties below the line for three months straight, and you get 30 days notice.
A paid member is an account whose own card was charged at least $5 for a pass in the last 30 days. Free seats and patrons do not move the count.

warmCold.title: WARM / COLD

blocks.head: Why is my pour cold?
blocks.body: Because the bar is quiet. Every tap is its own GPU, and a GPU nobody is using gets switched off. Taps scale to zero when the bar is quiet, so a cold pour takes about 30 seconds. After that the tap stays warm for a minute past your last message. Reply inside the minute and it stays warm. Take longer and the next pour is cold again: another wait, and the cold minimum.

blocks.head: A cold tap means not enough people are drinking here yet.
blocks.body: While you read and type, the tap you woke is sitting warm and already paid for. The next drinker on that tap shares it, and rides on it for nearly nothing. Two drinkers on one tap: the pour costs us about half. Four: about a quarter. That is the whole trick, and it is the only one.

blocks.head: More drinkers, warmer taps, cheaper pours. For everyone.
blocks.body: So drink from the house pours. They are marked. They are the taps most likely to be warm. Every drinker who follows the crowd makes the pour cheaper for the crowd. LAST CALL is the schedule that hands it back.

minimumPour.head: Minimum pour.
minimumPour.body: Every pour holds a tap for a minute, so every pour costs at least a minute: 1.2 / 1.5 / 2.5 cents by shelf. Waking a cold tap costs about double: 2.5 / 3 / 5 cents. Reply within a minute with a normal-sized context and you will not notice either. Short prompts, or long pauses between messages, and you will.

warmCold.shared: Taps are shared. Each tap is one GPU running one model; a few members may be served by the same tap at the same time. That sharing is what lowers the cost.

reducedFee.title: FINANCIAL ACCESSIBILITY & REDUCED FEE APPLICATION
reducedFee.headline: Can't swing it? There is a form.
reducedFee.sub: Same taps. Same tab. Lower price.
reducedFee.tableNote: Per month. Each line is its own price. On the house is the Well pass only, and those seats open only when the pool can fund them.
how: Six fields. No documents. A person reads it. Student, between jobs, bad exchange rate, disability, whatever it is: one or two sentences.
Approved for six months. We write to you two weeks before it ends. It never rolls over to a higher price on its own: ask again, pick the standard price, or let it lapse.
reducedFee.whoPays: Who pays for it: patrons. Their rounds go into the house pool. The pool pays the difference between your price and the standard price, and it is set aside for your full six months the day you are approved. Top Shelf reduced seats open last. Eligibility is financial only.
reducedFee.cap: Reduced seats are capped: one in four once the bar has twelve members, three seats until then. This is not a sale. It is a different price for people who need one.
reducedFee.queueNotice: READ THIS FIRST. The bar is not open and the pool is empty tonight. Applying now puts you on the waiting list, in the order applications arrive. Nothing is charged. No seat exists until the doors open and the pool can fund it.

tour.end: END OF THE BAR. GET ON THE LIST?

items.a: No. Nothing is for sale. The prices are the prices at opening, our best guess at cost. Open a tab and we write when the doors open.

items.q: Is this the cheapest way to run an uncensored model?
items.a: No. If you chat for hours a day, or run 16k of context all evening, a flat-rate host will cost you less and you should go there. Small models especially are cheaper almost anywhere else. We are for people who want these exact bottles, on a tap shared with a handful of drinkers instead of a crowd, from scripts and apps as well as chat, and who would rather see a meter than a queue.

A model whose refusals were cut out after training. Abliteration is one way to do it; the maker's Heretic pass is another; some of the merges are simply built from uncensored parts. Not every bottle had the same treatment. Each card prints what that bottle's own label says, and links to the maker's page.
One builder makes nine of the ten; the guest tap is from another cellar. Each card links to the maker's own page. We are not affiliated with any of them.

items.q: Can I point scripts and apps at it?
items.a: Yes. It is an API. The tab and the per-pass request limits are the limit.

items.q: Why does a long chat drain faster than a short one?
items.a: Your client resends the whole conversation each turn and we bill it as input each turn. Trim the context and the tab lasts longer.

items.q: Why did my tab move when I only said hello?
items.a: Minimum pour. Every pour holds a tap for a minute, so every pour costs at least a minute. See WARM / COLD.
The thinking is output. It is billed as output, including thinking your client hides. Six of the ten taps think: mini, reason, the three 27Bs and the flagship.
The tap was cold. Taps scale to zero when the bar is quiet, and a tap goes cold 60 seconds after its last request. The sign shows which taps are warm.

items.q: Does my unused tab roll over?
items.a: No. Rounds you bought do, for a year.

items.q: Do I get a tap to myself?
items.a: No. Taps are shared. Each tap is one GPU running one model, and a few members may be served by it at the same time. That sharing is what lowers the cost.
This page: what the Privacy page says, and no more. The API: nothing is promised here. Its policy gets written down before the doors open. Until it is, assume nothing.
No. It is a fiction-writing and developer API, 18 and over, with an acceptable-use policy. Read it.
